name: Height Of A Generic Tree

editorial:
The problem here deals with calculating the height of the given input generic tree. The point here to note is that we are calculating the height of the tree with respect to edges and not with respect to nodes i.e. for this problem the height of the tree is the maximum number of edges between the root node and the leaf node.

The basic idea here is to get the height of all the root children nodes and add 1 to the maximum height to get the resultant result. So we would use recursion to call recursively all the children of the node keeping the faith that the recursion result will tell us the height of the subtree.

Let us consider the following example:

We can observe here that the height of the tree is 3 (w.r.t. edges).

Now let us try to verify this with the help of our recursive solution.

ans = maximum of(height(20), height(30), height(40)) + 1

ans = maximum of({maximum of(height(50), height(60)) + 1}, {maximum of(height(70), height(80), height(90))}, {maximum of(height(100)) + 1}) + 1

ans = maximum of({maximum of(0, 0) + 1}, {maximum of(0, height(80), 0}, {maximum of(0) + 1}) + 1

ans = maximum of({0+1}, {(maximum of(height(100), height(120)) + 1) + 1}, {0+1}) + 1

ans = maximum of({1}, {(maximum of(0, 0) + 1) + 1}, {1}) + 1

ans = maximum of({1}, {1 + 1}, {1}) + 1

ans = maximum of({1}, {2}, {1}) + 1

ans = 2 + 1 = 3

Hence our result is verified.

Note: In the above verification though we have called recursion simultaneously in practicality recursion is called sequentially, here it would be in the order height(20) then height(30) then height(40).

Below is the implementation in Java:

private static int height(Node node) {
                                    int h = -1;
                                    for (Node child : node.children) {
                                        int ch = height(child);
                                        h = Math.max(h, ch);
                                    }
                                    h += 1;
                                    return h;
                                }

Time Complexity: O(n)

The time complexity for the function is linear as we are traversing every node in the tree to consider its node height.

Space Complexity: O(logn)

The space complexity for the function is approximately equal to the height of the tree due to the recursion stack.
